gaps.text: In-line measurement of Product temperature with temperature sensor at the probe position

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: NIR reflection and Raman spectra from the same sampling spot are synchronised to a common time step and merged into one augmented matrix for PLS regression. Each method keeps its own calibration and diagnostics, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out batches or it is dropped.)
In-line accuracy, response time and calibration performance for this specific opaque, concentrated product are not in the supplied sources; they must come from the comparison experiment.
The varying temperature and texture will not prevent a usable in-line measurement.

items.finding: The review states that the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for NIR and MIR measurements of aqueous solutions, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: Since the product is aqueous and temperature varies, the comparison experiment should record product temperature at the probe position and test whether temperature variation degrades the NIR models, e.g. by including temperature as a variable or checking residuals against temperature.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns NIR/MIR of aqueous solutions in laboratory setups with tempered holders, not in-line probes on an opaque concentrated dairy product, so the magnitude of the effect here is unknown.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: In this FT-IR and Raman study, temperature was deliberately varied, alongside concentrations and ionic strength, to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This supports building temperature variation into the calibration design of the comparison experiment rather than controlling it, so the in-line model can be tested under the temperature range the production line actually shows.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a lithium-recycling liquid-liquid extraction process with a different matrix and analytes, so the achievable robustness to temperature may not carry over to a concentrated milk product.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E03 ¶19

items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as the simplest combination method, where variables from different sources are concatenated one after the other into a new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This matches the planned approach of merging synchronised NIR and Raman spectra into one augmented matrix for PLS regression, and suggests it is a reasonable starting point for the comparison experiment.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The review discusses fusion in general PAT contexts; it does not establish that low-level fusion of NIR reflection and Raman works for an opaque concentrated dairy product in-line.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31

items.finding: A food analytical study combining Raman and FT-IR data showed that in some situations instrument complementarity alone was not sufficient to improve the prediction of several quality attributes.
items.how_it_applies: This is a reason to apply the planned acceptance rule strictly: the fused model must outperform the best single method on held-out batches, otherwise it should be dropped as foreseen.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited example used Raman with FT-IR rather than NIR reflection, and was a food analytical study, so the outcome for this NIR-Raman pairing is unknown.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E02 ¶36

items.finding: The review states that before fusing data from multiple sources it is essential to evaluate each dataset's contribution to the model and its complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: The comparison experiment should therefore first characterise the single-method NIR and Raman calibrations and diagnostics before building the fused model, so each method's contribution can be judged.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general methodological recommendation from a review, not a demonstrated result for this product or for in-line NIR-Raman fusion.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E02 ¶82

items.finding: Raman spectroscopy is frequently applied in bioprocessing because of its high selectivity and low water interference, despite relatively long measurement times.
items.how_it_applies: Low water interference is relevant for an aqueous, opaque product where NIR water bands dominate, but the noted long measurement times mean the achievable response time must be measured in the experiment, not assumed.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns upstream biopharmaceutical processing, not in-line dairy measurement, and says nothing about accuracy or response time for this product.

citation.quote: Raman spectroscopy is frequently applied in upstream processing in research and industry due to its high selectivity and low water interference [55] despite the relatively long measurement times.
citation.label: E01 ¶20

items.finding: The study notes that in-line methods require maintenance such as calibration and handling of sensor drift and aging, which it addressed by checking the baseline in each cycle and monitoring drift.
items.how_it_applies: This supports planning ongoing calibration maintenance and drift monitoring in the comparison experiment, since laboratory checks are retained and can serve as reference for detecting drift.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The approach relies on recurring pure-component phases in that specific process, which a continuous milk production line may not have, so an equivalent drift-check routine must be designed separately.

citation.quote: Potential typical drawbacks of any in-line method are maintenance efforts like calibration, and actions to sensor drift and aging could be easily overcome by checking the baseline in each cycle of pure component phases of process operation and monitoring any drift in order to be able to react.
citation.label: E03 ¶72
